generalfeedback:
In order to solve this problem we will have to use the method of integration by parts <hint>calc_int_methods_parts</hint> as follows:

Let \(u = {{CT:2}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:3}} d{{CT:1}}\).

Then \(du = {{CT:4}} d{{CT:1}}\) and \(v = {{CT:5}}\).

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:2}}{{CT:5}} - \int {{CT:5}}{{CT:4}}d{{CT:1}}
 \end{array}\]

In order to solve \[\int {{CT:5}}{{CT:4}}d{{CT:1}}\] we need to apply integration by parts again difining

\(u = {{CT:6}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:7}} d{{CT:1}}\).

Then \(du = {{CT:8}} d{{CT:1}}\) and \(v = {{CT:9}}\).

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:5}}{{CT:4}}d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:6}}{{CT:9}} - \int {{CT:9}}[{{CT:8}}d{{CT:1}}] \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:6}}{{CT:9}} - \int {{CT:10}}d{{CT:1}} \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:6}}{{CT:9}} + {{CT:11}}
 \end{array}\]

Hence,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:2}}{{CT:5}} - \left({{CT:6}}{{CT:9}} + {{CT:11}}\right) \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:12}}
 \end{array}\]

Thus,

\[{{CT:13}} = {{CT:14}}\]

And so,

\[{{CT:15}} = {{CT:16}}\]
